content_voiceover: This algorithm from the Taiwan MPN Working Group outlines management of polycythemia vera. Every patient, regardless of risk category, gets aggressive phlebotomy targeting hematocrit below forty five percent in both men and women, plus low dose aspirin, one hundred milligrams daily, if there's no contraindication. Risk stratification then splits patients into low risk, no history of thrombosis and age sixty or under, versus high risk, history of thrombosis or age over sixty. Low risk patients are managed with phlebotomy and aspirin alone, plus aggressive control of cardiovascular risk factors like hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and smoking. Cytoreduction can still be considered in low risk patients for specific indications, poor phlebotomy tolerance, symptomatic splenomegaly, severe symptoms, very high blood counts, symptomatic iron deficiency from phlebotomy, or new thrombosis or bleeding. High risk patients get cytoreduction added, first line hydroxyurea starting at five hundred milligrams twice daily, titrated up to two grams a day, with ropeginterferon alpha two b as an alternative to consider. If patients develop hydroxyurea intolerance or resistance, ropeginterferon becomes the next step. Patients with a history of arterial thrombosis should have twice daily aspirin or another antiplatelet agent considered, while those with venous thrombosis history get systemic anticoagulation added. Finally, ruxolitinib is reserved for severe, protracted pruritus or marked splenomegaly not otherwise controlled.
keypoints: All PV patients get phlebotomy to hematocrit under forty five percent plus low dose aspirin
Low risk equals no thrombosis history and age under sixty, high risk is thrombosis history or age over sixty
First line cytoreduction in high risk PV is hydroxyurea, with ropeginterferon as an alternative
Arterial thrombosis history favors twice daily antiplatelet therapy, venous history favors anticoagulation
Ruxolitinib is reserved for refractory pruritus or marked splenomegaly
keypoint_voiceover: The core PV algorithm to remember is phlebotomy to hematocrit under forty five percent plus aspirin for everyone, with hydroxyurea or ropeginterferon added for high risk patients defined by age over sixty or prior thrombosis. Reserve ruxolitinib for refractory symptoms like pruritus or splenomegaly rather than as routine cytoreduction.
